episodes.206468: A troughing pattern from the Pacific brought in a late season monsoon burst of moisture to the Desert Southwest. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed over portions of the state with more locally heavy rainfall events occurring from the abundant monsoon moisture. Flash flooding was observed in several locations ranging from near El Malpais south of Grants, NM, in Navajo Nation west of Crownpoint, and in Tijeras east of Albuquerque. One woman was reportedly swept away from flash flooding south of Gallup near Red Rock.
episodes.206522: An early season low pressure system moved into southeastern California and cut off from the main steering flow.  Leftover monsoon moisture from the subtropics combined with the stalled low pressure system and brought a 4 day period of severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.206578: A stalled frontal boundary remained just off the coast of Eastern North Carolina through the day on the twenty-nineth. Along this stalled boundary widespread shower and thunderstorm activity developed with an isolated storm becoming strong in nature. This brought a threat for waterspouts, primarily along the Crystal Coast.
episodes.206616: A trough to the west, coupled with the effects of moist upslope flow, helped trigger scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across far West Texas and Southeast New Mexico throughout the day on September 28th. While no severe weather was reported, ample moisture and terrain effects resulted in at least one instance of flash flooding in the Davis Mountains and one instance of flooding due to runoff near Carlsbad.
episodes.206951: A fairly weak cutoff low slowly ejected northward through the area over the course of several days. This feature in combination with sufficient moisture created an environment that supported several days of shower and thunderstorm development. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rainfall and flash flooding, as well as some strong wind gusts.
episodes.207713: A late season monsoonal moisture push to the Rio Grande combined with an upper trough moving northeast through the Four Corners region brought severe thunderstorms to parts of Otero County.
episodes.207873: Low pressure moved very slowly east from the eastern Pacific across the Mojave Desert, triggering scattered thunderstorms for a few days. Several storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.207907: As Summer began winding down, a strong trough pushed a cold front through southeast Oregon and southwest Idaho. The timing coincided with peak instability, allowing thunderstorms to form as the front passed. These storms exhibited locally heavy rainfall, but even more significant local wind gusts observed in southeast Oregon.

events.narrative: Public estimated 2 feet of water from Webber Creek flowing over the road entering Geronimo Estates.
Public reported water flowing over Fire Control Road in at least 8 spots west of Geronimo Estates.
The Agua Fria below Ash Creek county river gauge (54897) measured a 3.75 foot rise between 5:00 pm and 5:50 pm MST with a peak streamflow of 3,354 cfs.
Public reported a rapid 4 foot water rise in Pine Creek at Tonto Natural Bridge State Park.

Eddy County Office of Emergency Management reported flooding from higher terrain runoff on West Loop Road between Hidalgo Street and Lea Street. The total time of occurrence is estimated. No damage was reported.

Rome airport observed gusts near 60 mph for about 5 minutes as a thunderstorms gust front move through. Sustained winds were between 36-44 mph at the same time. This occurred shortly before an even stronger gust occurred at Burns Junction.

A thunderstorm developed near Burns Junction shortly after the Rome storm, and produced even stronger wind. The mesonet near Burns Junction recorded gusts over 60 mph for about 10 minutes, with a peak gust of 71 mph. Sustained winds were still near 40 mph, speaking to the quick moving nature of the winds.
A post on social media showed flooded roadways in some neighborhoods on Kirtland Air Force Base. Time and location are an estimate based on radar and the photos in the social media post.

A woman driving home on New Mexico Highway 602 about 5 miles south of Gallup was swept away in floodwaters, according to Navajo Nation and New Mexico State Police. Tragically, her deceased body was found after a five day search and rescue operation in nearby areas.
Heavy rain in headwaters resulted in the development of a flood wave in the Dirty Devil, with the wave cresting at 604 cfs at The Dirty Devil at Poison Springs above Hanksville gauge.

The Apache Mesonet site recorded a peak gust of 58 mph.
There was minor flooding of Highway 168 at Gilbert Pass.
